svg.title: Maknae system interfaces
svg.desc: DoDAF SV-1 systems interface description for Maknae.
svg.text: Every interface carries a status. 8 peer interfaces exist and 3 host-platform controls act on the daemon. 2 are ratified by ADR-0006 and
NOT implemented — that ADR carries its own banner saying so. 1 is a one-line marker crate with no interface at all.
Solid violet is a built peer interface; dashed grey is not built; dotted gold is a mandatory host control, which enforces rather than exchanges.
identity: the invoking uid; the OS is the authority
AF_UNIX stream at /run/maknae/maknaed.sock, group-gated on bind; mutual mTLS, TLS 1.3 pinned; SCM_RIGHTS carries the
identity: plane leaf certificate, URI-SAN — MACHINE identity only
HTTPS via vaultrs/reqwest; AppRole login, then pki sign; TLS negotiated (1.2 floor), FIPS suite set asserted
HTTPS; the user's own userpass token (`maknae login`) mints the cli-plane leaf and reads the user's key only
HTTPS; wrapping lookup + unwrap of the user's wrapping token, after the seal is opened; no Vault identity
identity: none — the wrapping token is the only credential presented
append-only write + fsync on a blocking worker; the reply is gated on the append
identity: enrolled remote subject, asserted by the gateway
machine channel; the gateway ASSERTS the principal to the PDP
identity: gateway's own scoped machine credential — never the daemon's plane/kernel identity
HTTPS, the user's key as bearer
identity: the user's own provider API key, unwrapped for this one call
AF_UNIX stream at egress.socket_path (default /run/maknae-egress/egress.sock); one connection per decided request; the
peer's uid is checked before the first write
identity: the Egress Daemon's uid, from the socket's peer credentials
none — maknae-mcp is a one-line CRATE_MARKER
SELinux policy_module(maknae, 1.0.0) confines maknaed_t, with separate types for etc, private, secret, audit and
runtime, plus maknae_vault_port_t on the outbound leg. Debian and Ubuntu get an equivalent AppArmor 3.x profile.
identity: the daemon's own domain — maknaed_t, entered via maknaed_exec_t
Execution is gated by fapolicyd's rpmdb trust backend; the rpm-installed binary is trusted automatically. NO per-file
trust record is shipped, deliberately — a static path/size/sha256 record goes stale on every rebuild, and a bare path
identity: package provenance, not a credential
packaging/common/maknae.fapolicyd.trust — verified on a STIG-hardened enforcing Rocky 10 host
StandardOutput=journal, StandardError=journal, SyslogIdentifier=maknaed. This is the DIAGNOSTIC channel and is not the
audit trail — AU-3 records go to the append-only sink at I5, on a path whose write gates the reply.
Stated negatives — surfaces that do not exist
Read this document for attack surface and an absent one looks like an oversight. These are absent on purpose.
No inbound network interface exists. Nothing in the tree binds a TCP or UDP port; the only bind is UnixListener::bind
on the client plane. Every occurrence of :8200 is a Vault address to DIAL.
There is nothing to ingress-filter, which is why no firewalld, nftables or ufw profile ships. #117's gateway is the
first inbound listener, and the first thing that will need one.
crates/maknae-kernel/src/run.rs:1879 — PlaneListener::bind on an AF_UNIX path
Every network flow is EGRESS — to Vault, and from the Egress Daemon to the provider — and each is constrained by
something narrower than a firewall rule.
SELinux authorizes each connect per DOMAIN, where a host firewall rule would authorize it per HOST: name_connect on
maknae_vault_port_t for maknaed_t and maknae_egress_t, and the provider leg (http_port_t) for maknae_egress_t alone. A
packet filter cannot express 'this process and no other'.
Reaching the client plane requires a local account in the gated group, not a route.
The socket is filesystem-mediated: group-gated at bind, then mutual mTLS over it. A network position buys nothing, so
perimeter controls are not the boundary that matters here.
